locations.name: Columbus Circle
locations.factShort: Columbus Circle is a traffic circle and busy road junction in the New York City borough of Manhattan, at the intersection of Eighth Avenue, Broadway, Central Park South (West 59th Street), and Central Park West, at the southwest corner of Central Park.

locations.name: Industry City
locations.factShort: Industry City (also Bush Terminal) is a historic intermodal shipping, warehousing, and manufacturing complex on the Upper New York Bay waterfront in the Sunset Park neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City.

locations.name: The Court Square Clock Tower
locations.factShort: One Court Square, also known as the Citicorp Building or the Citigroup Building, is a 50-story, 673-foot office tower in Long Island City, Queens, across the East River from Manhattan in New York City, United States. It was completed in 1989 and designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill for Citigroup.

locations.name: Concrete Plant Park
locations.factShort: The Bronx River is a river approximately 24 miles long, flowing through southeastern New York in the United States and draining an area of 38.4 square miles. It is named after colonial settler Jonas Bronck.

locations.name: Todt Hill
locations.factShort: Todt Hill ( TOHT) is a 401-foot-tall hill formed of serpentine rock on Staten Island, New York. It is the highest natural point in the five boroughs of New York City and the highest elevation on the entire Atlantic coastal plain from Florida to Cape Cod.
